gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Approachable and unfussy, Noto Sans Lydian sits beneath Azonix. Its capitals barely clear the lowercase and its openings gape like a sprung paper clip, so text flows smoothly, while Azonix's bowls never thin.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-nag-munda: Noto Sans Nag Mundari has lowercase that rivals its capitals. Azonix does its best work with a unit-width stroke throughout, while this plain sans does its best with curves that look half unwrapped.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Contemporary through and through, Noto Sans Nushu towers. Its terminals hang far from the stroke body while Azonix, bent like rope or tubing, anchors the top, so the plain sans below feels open beside it.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Rounded wire up top, solid blocks of words below, with Azonix leading in a commanding voice. Noto Sans Ol Chiki sits beneath it, curve tails held well back from the body, a clean counterweight.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Full bowls, stern manner: Azonix never thins its curves at the sides. Noto Sans Siddham follows with a friendly, large central band and an s whose ends hang far from the spine.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Bent-tubing letters up top, rope-bight curves below: Azonix commands and Noto Sans Sunuwar leaves daylight in every curve. Short ascender stems keep the plain sans body compact beside it.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Noto Sans Tai Viet pulls terminals back from where each curve closes, plus short ascenders and a tall x-height. Unshaded Azonix lines against an approachable plain sans: that is the draw.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-tamil-sup: Contemporary and clean, Noto Sans Tamil Supplement stands tall. Azonix does its best work in plain constant-width lines, while the body does best with round forms like open parentheses in a tall, stocky band.
